$comment: CROSS-PLATFORM CONFORMANCE VECTORS for the thread-replies latest-N read model.
Contract: RFC 043 Appendix B addendum — getLatestNReplies / listenLatestNReplies.
Web (packages/web/tests/threadRepliesReadModel.test.ts) and KMP run THIS SAME FILE.
@赵梓淇's equal-verdict gate (#731 discipline): identical input vectors must produce
byte-identical snapshots on both platforms. A divergence is a contract violation, not
The two invariants under test, and why they are silent when broken:
1. ORDER BY SEQ — a late/reordered frame carries an OLDER seq. A naive unshift would
promote a stale reply into the newest slot, and the preview would lie about what
2. DEDUPE BY IDENTITY (messageId), against a FIXED snapshot seam — never by seq
magnitude. A running high-water mark looks equivalent and is not: two genuinely
new replies arriving out of order (9 before 8) make it discard 8 as 'old', and a
real reply vanishes forever with no error. (This is a bug I shipped and my own
permutation test caught — hence the vector `out_of_order_convergence`.)

cases.name: late_frame_does_not_lead_the_window
cases.why: A frame older than the whole window must not enter it, let alone lead it.

cases.name: out_of_order_convergence
cases.why: THE permutation property. Any arrival order of the same frames must converge to the same window. This is the vector that caught the running-watermark bug.

cases.name: out_of_order_convergence_control_in_order
cases.why: Control for the above: the in-order permutation must produce an identical window.

cases.name: reconnect_replay_is_a_no_op
cases.why: On reconnect the server replays history. Without the seam these duplicate into the window and inflate replyCount.

cases.name: replay_then_genuinely_new_reply_still_lands
cases.why: The seam must not block real new replies that follow a replay.

cases.name: duplicate_message_id_dropped_even_with_higher_seq
cases.why: Identity dedupe, not seq dedupe: a re-delivered message must not appear twice.

cases.name: reply_below_seam_ignored_even_when_window_has_room
cases.why: Guards against 'only apply the seam when the window is full' — an already-counted reply stays out regardless of room.

cases.name: empty_scope_ingests_first_reply_seam_stays_zero
cases.why: No snapshot was ever loaded, so the seam is 0 — and a live frame must never move it.
